content: A lesion is a term derived from the Latin word laesio, which translates to injury. It refers to any abnormal tissue present in or on an organism, typically resulting from disease or trauma. Lesions can arise from any process that causes tissue damage. For instance, a cancerous tumor itself is considered a lesion, but the surrounding tissue that is damaged by the tumor is also classified as a lesion. Traumatic events, such as electrocution or chemical burns, can lead to the formation of lesions. Certain diseases manifest with lesions, such as the characteristic skin deformities seen in chickenpox. Lesions may also result from metabolic processes, such as ulcers, or from autoimmune activity, as observed in various forms of arthritis. In some cases, lesions are intentionally created during neurosurgical procedures, such as the precise brain lesions used to treat epilepsy or other neurological disorders. It is important to note that lesions are not exclusive to animals or humans; plants can also exhibit lesions when damaged. Given the broad definition of lesions, their types and classifications are nearly limitless. Lesions are often categorized based on their specific characteristics. For example, lesions caused by cancer are classified as either malignant or benign. They may also be classified by their shape, such as the bullseye or target appearance of certain ulcers. The size of a lesion can be described as gross (visible to the naked eye) or histologic (requiring microscopic examination). Another classification system considers whether a lesion occupies space, such as a small area of the brain that has liquefied following a stroke. Some lesions have specialized names. For instance, Ghon lesions are found in the lungs of individuals with tuberculosis. The distinctive skin lesions caused by a varicella-zoster virus infection are referred to as chickenpox. Lesions affecting the teeth are commonly known as dental caries. Lesions are also frequently classified by their location, such as distinguishing between a skin lesion and a brain lesion.
